title: MONEY - the chapter opener, the currency systems, Tables 43-44
audit_comment: OA round twenty-three (capture pp. 73-75): the money opener prose, the monetary systems, the coin values and the T44 barter grid

banner.title: THE MONEY OPENER, THE CURRENCY DOCTRINE AND TABLES 43-44, printed capture pp. 73-75 - the OA money round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture alone for this range (the settling authority): the first Mistral-OCR capture session is unavailable above p. 33, so the cross-capture agreement check is impossible. No contested cells detected within the single source: the T43 conversion matrix pins as the coin-value consts - the fen-basis values with the printed cross ratios, including the ch'ao-tael equality (the yuan 5 fen, the ch'ao 100 fen or 20 yuan, the tael 100 fen, 20 yuan or one ch'ao, the ch'ien 1000 fen, 200 yuan, 10 ch'ao and 10 tael); the T44 grid pins as five barter rows in the ch'ien and tael value columns (the koku 5 ch'ien, the sheep or goat 5 tael, the horse 2 ch'ien, the common and silk bolts 1 and 3 ch'ien). OCR normalization: the systems prose reads "[x]" placeholders for the printed blanks ("one coin can buy [x] amount of rice") - they pin nothing numeric; the em dashes of the print read normally. The Starting Money prose and Table 45 (capture pp. 75-76) and the Gajin exchange prose with Table 46 (capture pp. 76-77) are deliberately left for the next rounds
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 84 closed, 151 open - the Currency prose, Table 43, Table 44 and the Chapter 5 parent (opens) boxes flip (census 558 -> 559); NEXT - R637: the Starting Money prose and Table 45 (Initial Character Funds), capture pp. 75-76, the class funds dice, prefix dgx (verify free), audit "R637 OA starting money audit", include after rules/oamoney.h

bools.name: dgwGoldNotCurrency
bools.comment: Coins prose (capture pp. 74-75): Kara-Tur uses copper, silver and paper currency - gold is not a proper form of currency and is reserved for artistic and craft purposes

bools.name: dgwCoinsPiercedAndStrung
bools.comment: Coins prose (capture p. 75): each coin is pierced through the center and threaded on cash strings, tucked in the sleeve - simplifying the carrying and the counting

bools.name: dgwChaoPaperNote
bools.comment: Ch'ao prose (capture p. 75): the ch'ao is a paper note, preferred when dealing in amounts of 100 fen or greater

bools.name: dgwChienHoarded
bools.comment: Ch'ien prose (capture p. 75): the ch'ien is rarely used in everyday transactions since it is awkward to carry, and is hoarded for times when the copper and paper money falls in value

bools.name: dgwNobleSpending
bools.comment: Opener prose (capture pp. 73-74): refined nobles support the arts, field armies, provide for followers, build public works, maintain households and give gifts; lesser status spends on clothing, equipment, lodgings and artistic tastes

bools.name: dgwSystemsDivergent
bools.comment: Systems prose (capture p. 74): Shou Lung prints paper money, T'u Lung mints regular coinage, Kozakura uses the coins of others, the warlords occasionally mint coins, and the barbarian tribes live without minted coins - barter and direct trade only

bools.name: dgwEstablishedCurrency
bools.comment: Established currency prose (capture p. 74): the government controls the minting with uniform coins backed by the imperial treasury, issues paper money beyond true value, oversees market prices, takes taxes in grain - barter uncommon, haggling expected for the larger purchases

bools.name: dgwRegularCurrency
bools.comment: Regular currency prose (capture p. 74): the coins are not always regular in size or shape, the value follows the metal content, weighing coins is not uncommon, the larger purchases run by barter - land via gems, art, services or a crop share

bools.name: dgwIrregularCurrency
bools.comment: Irregular currency prose (capture p. 74): foreign coins are used without prejudice, every coin is worth only its precious metal content, paper money is useless, wealth is measured by the goods and contracts held, and the legal systems enforce the contracts

bools.name: dgwPureBarter
bools.comment: Pure barter prose (capture p. 74): wealth is measured purely by the goods owned, contracts are generally not drawn, purchases trade equal value, haggling is a must, the legal systems stay informal and the reputation as dealer or cheat moves the prices

bools.name: dgwDmChoosesSystem
bools.comment: Systems prose (capture p. 74): characters normally deal with a single system - the DM picks by campaign area and may choose the simplest system so as not to slow the play

bools.name: dgwBarterUnitDoctrine
bools.comment: Barter units prose (capture p. 75): a barter unit is a set amount of goods seen as having a specific value - the farmer in koku of rice, the nomad in horses, the merchant in bolts of cloth

bools.name: dgwQualityVariesValue
bools.comment: Barter units prose (capture p. 75): the buying power of livestock and cloth varies greatly with the quality - the well-fed horse and the fine cloth fetch higher prices
